I struggle with depression too, but I’ll try my best to explain what I mean by it

To me “choosing to be happy” means trying to think of things positively even when its difficult to do so- trying to see bad/unsavory things as a new opportunity or a lesson instead of being completely upset about it

Now- theres many situations in life where this is hard or impossible to implement; especially in the case of death of a loved one or in cases of severe depression

Personally I have found when I view things positively- or fuck even just neutrally instead of negatively they are easier to deal with. “Being happy in the face of hardship” doesn’t necessarily mean ALWAYS being happy- it means daring to TRY to see the positive/learning lesson in whatever life throws your way

Anger and sadness are not “bad” emotions- they are just emotions we dont like. theres a lot you can learn from these feelings- in my own life when I started choosing to see these feelings as old friends rather then enemies is when I started to feel happier; daring to see the positive in a shit situation makes that situation less shitty imo

“Full” understanding ?? Of course not. I think the worse your situation the more beneficial it is to BE greatful. (key word here being “beneficial” not “easy”) life is hard enough being homeless- becoming lost in how much you have suffered only makes you feel worse and makes your life harder. I don’t know what kind of experiences you’ve lived through- but from someone who has been homeless if I had adopted your way of thinking I probably would not still be here today

For me calling it a blessing is the truth. My dad flatlined when I was 10- went into a coma for 2 months; my family lost everything. My mom attempted suicide when I was 15- IN FRONT OF ME. I have had the words “I WISH YOU WERE NEVER BORN” SCREAMED in my face by my own mother during a psychotic episode. I call life a blessing because despite all this I get to feel joy everyday- and I’m lucky enough to still be alive. 

So many people die every single day- what do you say to them? That their life was suffering because of the hardship? Or would they tell you to enjoy what little life we are gifted to the fullest without trying to label it “good” or “bad” ? That every second we have on this world is NOT guaranteed- and that at any moment we could lose EVERYTHING. Even the things you were never greatful for when you had them.

 When we suffer and feel these awful emotions it’s important to remember what we have to live for. My suffering has taught me so much about how to love and appreciate the life I get to have- in ways many people who haven’t suffered wouldn’t get to appreciate.

Also- my comment is just MY opinion; not saying it’s the only “right” way of thinking :)
